source.title: Cross-seed explainability using Procrustes-conditioned Joint End-to-end Top-K Sparse Autoencoders

record.file_problem: None; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates cross-seed SAE feature correlations and classification accuracy after SAE injection. It does not measure whether SAE reconstruction errors are linearly predictable, how error norms scale, whether larger SAEs fail on the same tokens, or any of the other specified dark-matter claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports feature-correlation and dead-feature results, which do not measure SAE reconstruction-error structure. It also reports classification accuracy changes after SAE injection; these are recorded under fits_no_version because the study does not compare those effects with random errors of equal size or measure model loss.
record.test_reason: The study trains Procrustes-aligned joint TopK end-to-end SAEs on BERT and measures cross-seed feature correlation, dead-feature rates and classification accuracy after SAE injection. It never measures the structure of the SAE error: no linear prediction of the error, no error-norm scaling across SAE sizes, and no comparison with equal-size random errors. It reports no circuit or steering loss without the error term, and does not test whether the error shrinks with architecture. It does not cite the dark-matter paper, so it neither tests nor uses the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Procrustes-conditioned joint end-to-end TopK SAEs produce more cross-seed universal features (r≥0.70) than post-hoc matched baselines. They find post-hoc rotation alone gives no consistent benefit, and SAE injection leaves accuracy essentially unchanged. They note the evaluation covers only one BERT family and has no comparison with Feature Aligned or Orthogonal SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a Procrustes-aligned joint Top-K SAE to improve cross-seed feature universality; it does not use the original dark-matter error analysis or its measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature-correlation results vary across datasets and SAE conditions; the appendix also reports different feature results with sentence-level mean pooling rather than per-token evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: Injecting TopK end-to-end SAE reconstructions at BERT layer 10 changes fine-tuned classification accuracy by under about 0.5 percentage points on all three datasets and all conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: End-to-end TopK SAE splicing preserves downstream classification accuracy in fine-tuned BERT classifiers.

record.problems: The study does not measure reconstruction-error structure or compare SAE-induced errors to random errors. Its downstream check is classification accuracy rather than loss. The main experiments use five seed pairs from one BERT model family; the appendix pooling experiment uses two seed pairs.
record.rows_left_out: None of the separately reported accuracy-change values from Tables 1 and C3 were left out. Matched independent-SAE entries have no separately reported accuracy-change value; the text says their reconstruction and accuracy change are identical to the index entries.

untested.parts: Whether SAE error is linearly predictable from the input activation; not measured.
Per-token error-norm predictability, shared failure contexts across SAE sizes, and persistence with scale; only one dictionary size (6,144) is used.
Loss under SAE splicing versus equal-norm random errors; only classification accuracy change is reported, with no random-error control.
Linear versus nonlinear error components and their response to further dictionary learning; not measured.
Circuit or steering analyses with and without the error term; the counterfactual study only tracks the activation of one feature.
Whether error or dark matter shrinks with end-to-end or TopK training; no reconstruction-error or FVU numbers are compared across conditions.

record.verdict_notes: Relation 'discusses' is a loose fit: the paper does not cite or discuss SAE dark matter at all. It is T6. The accuracy rows are correctly linked to 'none'. The paper is internally inconsistent about the accuracy baseline: Section 4 says the change is relative to the independent SAE, while the Table C3 caption says clean→SAE-hijacked and 'negative = improvement'. The sign and baseline of r1–r24 are therefore uncertain. All SST-2 entries are exactly 0.00%. The AuxK loss trains dead latents on the residual error, but no error-structure metric is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of input activations.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, shared failure contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
Whether reconstruction replacement harms model loss more than random errors of the same size. The paper reports classification accuracy changes after SAE injection, not this comparison.
Whether linear error contains unlearned features and nonlinear error resists further dictionary learning.
Whether SAE-feature-based circuit or steering analyses lose behavior when the error term is omitted.
Whether dark matter is an SAE-training artifact or shrinks with improved architectures or end-to-end training.
